copied_current_escalation_decisions.evidence: Proof 1.1 correctly derives the ordinary compact-source pi0 classification conditional on the main theorem and the independently reviewed smoothing lemma. Its stronger Statement covers every compact pair and arbitrary compact parameter spaces without the theorem parameter class or holonomic smooth-near-Q input. Weak equivalence alone does not provide that relative comparison. Proof 2.1 applies the family argument to P times M: source-rank data in M directions cannot be used as an immersion of that higher-dimensional product. Attempted closure by restricting to the defined smooth parameter products would change the promised scope and still require the unresolved main theorem. Sources consulted: exact local weak-equivalence definition and relative-homotopy definition, the current main theorem and Francis Lectures 5–6 relative comparison framework. Owner/Step-5b must choose an exact permitted-relative-data statement or supply an additional general-compact-pair mapping-space theorem, and resolve the main prerequisite. No unsupported richer classification is accepted; risk stays open.
